summary: Built M2-S02 (access, design-only, build_mode design-only, API 62.0 defaulted because plan.json carries no api_version). Four files under artefacts/M2-S02/: the PermissionSet Enterprise_Sales_Record_Types carrying two recordTypeVisibilities (Opportunity.Enterprise, Opportunity.Renewal) and nothing else; the Sales User profile overlay carrying exactly two layoutAssignments (to M1-S02's two layouts, in file-name form) and two recordTypeVisibilities at default=false; package.xml (PermissionSet + Profile, member 'Sales User' with its space); and deploy-order.md. The step's open question — does this set grant field access — is decided NO and recorded in deploy-order.md section 0: Q19 names the persona's access source as the pre-existing Sales Cloud permission set, the step inputs bind no field, and the set grants no objectPermissions so PSVP-FLS-01's shape is absent. The consequence is recorded as a deploy-time gap: FLS for the two new fields M1-S01 created (Discount__c, Approval_Status__c) is granted by no file in this build. All three declared checkers exit 0 on the first pass, zero repair passes; check-outputs ok.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 MEDIUM: every emitted element traces to a cited skill's metadata-examples fence, all three checkers exited 0 on the first pass and check-outputs is ok — but four Questions-to-Ask rows were answered by a documented skill default rather than from the plan (license left empty, hasActivationRequired=false, the post-deploy verification step, and the Person Account row via assumption A6), so question-coverage is partial and the HIGH row's last clause is not met.

dimensions_skipped.reason: Four deduplicated Questions-to-Ask rows had no answer in step inputs, the answered clarifications, the upstream artefacts or requirement.md, and were filled from the cited skill's own documented default: the permission set's license (left empty, which admin/permission-set-architecture documents as a deliberate choice), hasActivationRequired=false, the post-deploy verification step, and Person Accounts (plan assumption A6, itself a G1 default on unanswered Q41). None of the four changes which components ship; each changes one element or one line of the note.
dimensions_skipped.retry_hint: Ask the requester which user licence the 14 Sales User holders hold before deploy; if it is mixed, the empty <license> is correct and should be recorded as a decision rather than a default.

process_observations.observation: The plan split this step into two files for the right reason and said so in inputs.note before the builder opened a skill: a permission set can carry recordType + visible only, and layoutAssignments plus the default record type exist solely on Profile. The element split the skill documents and the split the plan declared agree exactly, so nothing had to be re-derived.

Both layout strings and both record-type names were copied character-for-character from M1-S01's and M1-S02's file names rather than retyped, and M1-S02's own deploy-order note had already flagged a mismatch there as INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY.

Field-level security for Opportunity.Discount__c and Opportunity.Approval_Status__c — the two fields M1-S01 created and M1-S02's layouts place — is granted by no file in this build. Three access files exist across all sixteen steps and none carries a fieldPermissions block, while MILESTONE-M1-REPORT.md records the same zero from the other side and points at 'M2-S01 / M2-S02'. On the day of the deploy the two fields are invisible to every rep and to the deploying admin, which reads as a layout bug.

evidence.query: outputs[] across plan.json steps matching permissionsets/ or profiles/

process_observations.observation: The step's own acceptance-test description for check_record_type_layouts.py quotes a planning fixture run that printed '0 finding(s) detected'; the same command over the same tree now prints 1 finding (RTL-MERGE-01 REVIEW on M1-S02's two identical layouts). The exit code and the declared 'exit 0' are unaffected because the checker is lenient without --strict, and the finding itself was already adjudicated at the M1 gate as open item O-M1S02-03 — but the quoted fixture no longer reproduces.

PSVP-FLS-02 (WARN, non-blocking) fires on the Sales User overlay because it carries zero object and field permissions and no PermissionSetGroup exists in the tree. The checker's own docstring calls the rule deliberately simplified — it asserts only that some group exists to be the claimed access source. This build designs no PSG at all and the access source is a pre-existing Sales Cloud permission set outside it, so a human should confirm the WARN is accepted rather than closed by inventing a group.

The Profile member and file stem are written as 'Sales User' with its space, per the step's manifest acceptance test. No cited file shows a space-carrying profile member, so the form follows from the stem-equals-member rule rather than from an example, and Q19's phrase 'the standard Sales User profile' is the only evidence the org's profile is named exactly that. Marked UNVERIFIED (2026-09-19) inline in deploy-order.md.
The step is built and has not been tested; three declared checkers plus the always-on xml and manifest checks and two manual rows are waiting.
